# grpc-dc-proxy

<!-- @generated by grpc-dc codegen. DO NOT EDIT. -->

A supported TCP <-> DataChannel proxy. grpc-dc clients
(browser tabs, native peers) connect over WebRTC
DataChannels; calls are bridged to real backends, so
unmodified backend servers become reachable from a browser
with no grpc-web proxy in the page path and no backend
changes. gRPC compression is terminated in the proxy; the
DataChannel wire is always uncompressed.

## Modes

| Mode | Backend | Status | Implementation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `http2-bridge` | HTTP/2 backend (h2c) | shipped | proxy/grpc-dc-proxy.mjs (Node, stdlib only) | Stock grpc-go / grpc-java / grpc-node server, unmodified; compression terminated in the proxy |
| `tcp-smoltcp` | Plain TCP via userspace stack (smoltcp) | spike | proxy/tcp-sidecar (Rust, smoltcp) | Userspace TCP termination over a packet transport; zero OS sockets in the proof |
| `http3-terminator` | HTTP/3 (QUIC) backend | spike | proxy/h3-terminator (Rust, quinn) | QUIC terminated in the proxy; streams bridged to a TCP backend |

## Client surfaces

- **Browser (JS + all Wasm languages)** — Signaling over WebSocket to the proxy, then the `grpc` DataChannel; the proxy is the only HTTP/2 speaker.
- **Native (all generated languages)** — Same exchange via the native WebRTC stacks, or file-based SDP in tests; identical proxy protocol.

## Run (HTTP/2 bridge)

    node proxy/grpc-dc-proxy.mjs --backend 127.0.0.1:50051 [--port 8090]

- `--backend host:port` — the stock HTTP/2 gRPC server (h2c).
- Clients signal through `ws://<proxy>/` with the starter
  offer/answer exchange (`{kind:"offer",sdp}` ->
  `{kind:"answer",sdp}`), then open the `grpc` DataChannel.
- `GET /healthz` returns `ok`.
- For remote browsers, put the proxy behind any HTTPS
  tunnel (e.g. `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8090`);
  pages must then use `wss://`.

## Test

    node --test proxy/proxy.test.mjs     # or: make test-proxy

Spins up a minimal HTTP/2 Echo backend and drives a
generated JS client over a real DataChannel through the
proxy: unary, server-streaming, and an INVALID_ARGUMENT
trailers-only case. The test also checks this spec's mode
table against the implementation (parity).

## Sidecar spikes

- `proxy/tcp-sidecar/` — smoltcp userspace TCP proof
  (`cargo test` in that crate; zero OS sockets).
- `proxy/h3-terminator/` — QUIC termination proof
  (`cargo test` in that crate; quinn, self-signed).

Both are standalone spikes today: packet/stream transport
is transport-agnostic, and carrying it over DataChannels
into the release gate is the follow-up.
